page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.2xlarge is a high clock speed, compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture using KVM hypervisor technology. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs through hyperthreading. The CPU allocation is dedicated and includes 33 MB of L3 cache along with support for vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512 (f, VNNI, BF16), AES, and FMA. The instance provides 16.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. It includes zero local storage and no GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent average performance across compute and processing workloads. Multi-core performance highlights include a stress-ng multi-core score of 8310.78, a Geekbench multi-core score of 4720.0, and static web serving throughput of 7.7 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 8.09 million operations per second. However, memory subsystem testing indicates performance trade-offs: PassMark memory score and large-block uncached memory read bandwidth (37.74 GB/sec) fall in the weak percentile category. Additionally, medium model (7B) LLM prompt processing and generation speeds are poor at 11.72 and 5.16 tokens per second respectively.

With a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high core frequency, ecs.c4.2xlarge provides qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory arrays or ephemeral local NVMe drives. Because the instance relies on network-attached storage, storage IOPS and latency depend on attached cloud disk options. The server is suited for build and compilation systems, web serving, batch computing, and lightweight key-value caching layers like Redis.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor operating at 3.2 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of memory and 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it includes advanced CPU extensions such as AVX-512 and 33 MB of L3 cache. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, requiring remote block storage for persistent data. Synthetic CPU benchmarks indicate solid average multi-core and single-core execution speeds, including 8.09 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.7 GB/sec web serving throughput. However, memory bandwidth benchmarks display weak relative throughput under uncached large-block operations. Providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, ecs.c4.2xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for compute-focused workloads, web serving, code compilation, and batch data processing where local NVMe throughput and high RAM capacity are not required.
